rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Competing proximate causes and intentions are governed by one superior divine cause and will, which orders their effects and alternately gives precedence to each.
rows.anchor: سبب واحد وإرادة واحدة حاكمة لا يقع إلا ما يريده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The traveler's wish to move and need to stop can conflict, yet both remain obedient to a higher will that coordinates them.
rows.anchor: علة الوقوف ربما تنازع علة الطي والحركة وتوقفها عن العمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Kursi is the level where conflicting causes separate and contend; the Arsh is their harmonized level, prior to it and related as general to particular, hidden to manifest.
rows.anchor: المقام الذي ينفصل به السببان المتنافيان وينشأ منه تنازعهما بمنزلة الكرسي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The throne and chair fit these levels: the chair displays a ruler's judgments through independent agents, while the throne preserves the king's unaltered judgment and gathers the agents' details inwardly.
rows.anchor: فإن الكرسي الذي يظهر فيه أحكام الملك من جهة عماله وأيديه العمالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Kursi as the apparent gate is where novel cosmic events emerge and detailed, dispersed particulars of creation appear; the Arsh is the inward gate containing their comprehensive forms.
rows.anchor: لأن الكرسي هو الباب الظاهر " الخ " فقوله " منه مطلع البدع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the cited terminology, knowledge of how means a thing's manner of arising from its causes, while existence means its complete being and beginning and return its first existence and endpoint.
rows.anchor: علم الكيف " كأن المراد بالكيف خصوصية صدور الشيء عن أسبابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Measure and limit refer to one idea: measure is a thing's own quantity, while limit describes it relative to another and bars intermixture; where is spatial relation.
rows.anchor: القدر والحد " المراد بهما واحد غير أن القدر حال مقدار الشيء بحسب نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Will and the attribute of will may be synonymous; alternatively, will names its origin and the attribute of will its particular character.
rows.anchor: والمشيئة وصفة الإرادة " هما واحد ويمكن أن يكون المراد بالمشيئة أصلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Knowledge of words concerns how their meanings connect naturally to external realities; motion and abstention concern acts and omissions in relation to entities.
rows.anchor: علم الألفاظ هو العلم بكيفية انتشاء دلالة الألفاظ بارتباطها إلى الخارج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, words, movement, and abstention together describe how commands and prohibitions arise from acts and omissions, and languages from realities with one source; abstention is relative stillness opposite motion.
rows.anchor: ويمكن أن يكون المراد بمجموع قوله " علم الألفاظ وعلم الحركات والترك " العلم بكيفية انتشاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in knowledge of how things are refers to the Arsh; the apparent doors of badaʾ refer to the Kursi, where one cosmic cause appears and cancels another's effect.
rows.anchor: والبداء ظهور سبب على سبب آخر وإبطاله أثره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Arsh and Kursi are related neighbors and one reality at levels of generality and detail; saying one carries the other is a figure of speech that helps scholars grasp subtle knowledge.
rows.anchor: العرش والكرسي جاران متناسبان بل حقيقة واحدة مختلفة بحسب مرتبتي الإجمال والتفصيل

rows.speaker: الصادق
rows.claim: Asked about God's throne being over water, the Imam rejects a literal account with God above it: that would make God borne and imply the bearer is stronger than Him.
rows.anchor: كذبوا، من زعم هذا فقد صير الله محمولا ووصفه بصفة المخلوقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Imam's alternative says God placed His religion and knowledge on the water before heaven, earth, jinn, humans, sun, or moon existed; the author takes the Arsh as knowledge and water as creation's origin, known before its details appeared.
rows.anchor: قال إن الله حمل دينه وعلمه الماء قبل أن تكون سماء أو أرض أو جن أو إنس

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Asked how far earth is from the Arsh, Ali answers: a servant's sincere profession that there is no god but God.
rows.anchor: سئل عن بعد ما بين الأرض والعرش. فقال قول العبد مخلصا لا إله إلا الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ali's answer echoes the ascent of good words and the elevation of righteous deeds: sincerely denying independent divinity in anything else turns one toward God's encompassing authority, the station of the Arsh.
rows.anchor: أخذه من قوله تعالى { إليه يصعد الكلم الطيب والعمل الصالح يرفعه }

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Asked the distance between earth and sky, Ali answers that it is the range of sight and the prayer of the oppressed.
rows.anchor: قد سئل عن بعد ما بين الأرض والسماء مد البصر ودعوة المظلوم

rows.speaker: الصادق
rows.claim: A report explains the Kaaba's square shape by its alignment with the square Bayt al-Maʿmur, itself square because it faces the square Arsh; the Arsh is square because Islam rests on four phrases.
rows.anchor: قال لأنها بحذاء البيت المعمور وهو مربع.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The four phrases express transcendence, praise, unifying transcendence and likeness, and supreme tawhid: God exceeds every description and limit; this returns the throne's meaning to knowledge.
rows.anchor: أولاها تتضمن التنزيه والتقديس والثانية التشبيه والثناء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other traditions call the Throne's treasures the Throne's treasures, describe Sad as a river flowing from its base, and place a basin with star-count cups at the clear horizon before it.
rows.anchor: أن آية الكرسي وآخر البقرة وسورة محمد من كنوز العرش

rows.speaker: الصادق
rows.claim: In a report on Nun and the Pen, God makes the pen from a Garden tree, turns a Garden river into ink, and orders it to record everything through Resurrection on a pure sheet; He seals the pen and places the hidden book in the Arsh.
rows.anchor: إن الله خلق القلم من شجرة في الجنة يقال لها الخلد، ثم قال لنهر في الجنة كن مدادا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the questioner presses for more explanation, the Imam says the pen and tablet are angels, showing that the description is a sensory analogy for intelligible realities.
rows.anchor: لما استزاد الراوي بيانا وأصر عليه قال عليه السلام القلم ملك واللوح ملك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says the reported images of all created things in the Arsh are the reality underlying the verse about creation's treasuries with God.
rows.anchor: أي وجود صور الأشياء وتماثيلها في العرش هو الحقيقة التي يبتنى عليها بيان الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author notes a related narration in the interpretation of the supplication “O You who made beauty manifest.”
rows.anchor: وفي معنى هذه الرواية ما ورد في تفسير دعاء " يا من أظهر الجميل "

rows.speaker: الصادق
rows.claim: Another report describes a thousand-year flight between two throne pillars, seventy thousand colors of light clothing the Arsh daily, and all things as a ring in a desert.
rows.anchor: والعرش يكسى كل يوم سبعين ألف لون من النور لا يستطيع أن ينظر إليه خلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ring-in-desert wording is also transmitted from the Prophet in Shiʿi and Sunni sources and is figurative; even light-ray circles could exceed any measured throne, so sensory scale approximates an intelligible reality.
rows.anchor: والأشياء كلها في العرش كحلقة في فلاة

rows.speaker: الرضا
rows.claim: A report explains circumambulation: after the angels' objection to a human vicegerent, they regret it and seek refuge at the Arsh; God establishes the fourth-heaven al-Durāḥ, then Bayt al-Maʿmur below and the Kaaba aligned with it, and Adam's circumambulation continues through his descendants.
rows.anchor: فلاذوا بالعرش واستغفروا فأحب الله عز وجل أن يتعبد بمثل ذلك العباد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author calls the report unusual; if Arsh means knowledge, the angels' retreat signifies admitting ignorance and returning knowledge to God, as in their declaration that they know only what He taught.
rows.anchor: سبحانك لا علم لنا إلا ما علمتنا إنك أنت العليم الحكيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most traditions mention one heavenly house, Bayt al-Maʿmur in the fourth heaven; since angels are Quranically sinless, the report's sin may mean awareness of a shortcoming.
rows.anchor: ومعظم الروايات تذكر في السماء بيتا واحدا وهو البيت المعمور في السماء الرابعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Kaaba's alignment with Bayt al-Maʿmur is spiritual rather than physical: the Arsh and Kursi encompass the heavens and earth, so a physical container cannot be spatially aligned with what it contains.
rows.anchor: فالظاهر أنه محاذاة معنوية لا حسية جسمانية

rows.speaker: الصادق
rows.claim: A report depicts four throne bearers as a human, rooster, lion, and bull who seek provision for humans, birds, beasts, and livestock; the bull lowered its head when Israel worshipped the calf, and they become eight at Resurrection.
rows.anchor: أن حملة العرش أحدهم على صورة ابن آدم يسترزق الله لولد آدم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Similar reports are numerous; only one report the author found mentions bearers of the Kursi, which he discussed under the Throne Verse in al-Baqara.
rows.anchor: وهو الخبر الوحيد الذي يذكر للكرسي حملة - فيما عثرنا عليه -

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another report names eight throne bearers: Noah, Abraham, Moses, and Jesus from earlier communities, and Muhammad, Ali, Hasan, and Husayn from later ones.
rows.anchor: فأما الأربعة من الأولين فنوح وإبراهيم وموسى وعيسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With the Arsh understood as knowledge, both angels and other beings can be described as its bearers; traditions support this interpretation, while apparent bodily descriptions are read figuratively.
rows.anchor: بناء على تفسير العرش بالعلم لا ضير في أن تعد أربعة من الملائكة حملة له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No reliable report establishes a physical throne-shaped Arsh placed on the seventh heaven; the first cited report contradicts that conception.
rows.anchor: وأما كون العرش جسما في هيئة السرير موضوعا على السماء السابعة فمما لا يدل عليه حديث

rows.speaker: الصادق
rows.claim: On the creation of the heavens and earth in six days, a report glosses the six days as six periods.
rows.anchor: في ستة أوقات

rows.speaker: الحسن العسكري
rows.claim: Asked about God's command before and after, the Imam says God commands before He issues an order and afterward does whatever He wills; the narrator connects this to God's possession of creation and command, and the Imam confirms the link.
rows.anchor: لله الأمر من قبل أن يأمر ومن بعد أن يأمر ما يشاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's ownership of creation and command is absolute before and after its exercise, unlike human ownership, which ends once an owned matter is acted upon.
rows.anchor: يفيد إطلاق الملك قبل الصدور وبعده لا كمثلنا حيث نملك الأمر

rows.speaker: محمد
rows.claim: A Prophetic report says self-congratulation for a good deed without thanking God voids it, and claiming servants independently possess any part of God's command rejects revelation.
rows.anchor: من لم يحمد الله على ما عمل من عمل صالح وحمد نفسه فقد كفر وحبط ما عمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here disbelief through self-admiration means ingratitude for God's favor or denying that good deeds belong to God; denying servants any share of command targets independent, not derivative, authority.
rows.anchor: والمراد بنفي كون شيء من الأمر للعباد نفي الجعل بنحو الإستقلال دون التبعي

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: Maysar is told that the earth had been corrupt, then God revived it through His Prophet, in explanation of the prohibition against corrupting it after its reform; al-Ayyashi transmits a mursal version from Abu Abd Allah.
rows.anchor: إن الأرض كانت فاسدة فأحياها الله عز وجل بنبيه

rows.speaker: محمد
rows.claim: Abu Musa relates the Prophet's rain parable: receptive soil grows plentiful vegetation, soil that retains water benefits people who drink, water, and plant, while barren ground retains no water or growth; these represent people who learn and teach the guidance, and those who refuse it.
rows.anchor: مثل ما بعثني الله به من الهدى والعلم كمثل الغيث الكثير أصاب أرضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These verses summarize Moses' dealings with Pharaoh after his call: he urges worship of God and Israel's release, brings successive signs, is saved with his people, and sees Pharaoh drowned and Israel inherit the blessed land.
rows.anchor: تشتمل على إجمال ما جرى بينه عليه السلام وبين فرعون وقومه أيام إقامة موسى بينهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh's chiefs incite him to kill Moses and his people; Pharaoh says their murder is unnecessary because he already dominates them and can restore the earlier killing of sons and enslavement of women.
rows.anchor: هذا إغراء منهم لفرعون وتحريض له أن يقتل موسى وقومه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The chiefs' claim that Moses would leave Pharaoh and his gods intensifies the call for murder: they say Moses and his followers would abandon Pharaoh and his deities and corrupt the land.
rows.anchor: وقولهم { ويذرك وآلهتك } تأكيد لتحريضهم إياه على قتلهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh claimed divinity and enslaved people while also worshipping other gods; historical rulers could be worshipped by their subjects yet themselves revere ancestors and idols, and polytheistic gods could have subordinate gods.
rows.anchor: وفيه دلالة على أن فرعون كما كان يدعي الألوهية، ويستعبد الناس لنفسه كان يعبد آلهة أخرى

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some take Pharaoh's statements that he is the highest lord and knows no other god to mean he worshipped no deity and ordered his people to worship only him; a reported reading instead means “your worship.”
rows.anchor: ولذلك قال بعضهم إنه كان دهريا لا يعترف بصانع ويأمر قومه بترك عبادة الآلهة مطلقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author instead reads Pharaoh as denying a separate patron deity for the Egyptian people, not as asserting that no god exists; the continuation develops this reading from the surrounding context.
rows.anchor: لكن الأوجه أنه كان يريد بقوله { ما علمت لكم من إله غيري } نفى إله يخص قومه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement “I know no god for you but me” denies knowledge of another god, not the existence of one; the context says Pharaoh doubted whether he was Moses' god.
rows.anchor: فظاهرها أنه كان يشك في كونه إلها لموسى، وأن معنى قوله { ما علمت لكم من إله غيري } نفي العلم

rows.speaker: الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Razi argues Pharaoh could not rationally believe himself creator or persuade a large assembly that he was; he proposes Pharaoh denied a creator, credited stars with governing the world, and called himself his people's benefactor, while worshipping stellar idols.
rows.anchor: بل الأقرب أن يقال إنه كان دهريا ينكر وجود الصانع، وكان يقول مدبر هذا العالم السفلي هو الكواكب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects al-Razi's account: polytheistic gods govern aspects of the world rather than create it, atheists do not worship stars, and Sabians who worship stars do not deny a creator.
rows.anchor: بل الحق أن فرعون - كما تقدم - كان يرى نفسه ربا لمصر وأهله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh regarded himself as Egypt's and its people's lord, denying that they were governed by another deity; he did not deny that God created them or the world.
rows.anchor: لا أنهم أو غيرهم من العالم ليسوا مخلوقين لله سبحانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh promises to resume earlier persecution by killing Israelite sons and retaining their women for service; his claim of dominance reassures the chiefs and calms their agitation.
rows.anchor: وعد منه للملأ من قومه أن يعيد إلى بني إسرائيل تعذيبه السابق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses urges Israel to seek God's help toward liberation from Pharaoh's enslavement and to endure the threatened torments; patience leads to good and relief, grounded in God's ownership of the earth.
rows.anchor: بعث لبني إسرائيل واستنهاض لهم على الاستعانة بالله على مقصدهم وهو التخلص من إسارة آل فرعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh owns no land to grant or withhold: God gives it to whom He wills, and His established way grants a good outcome to the God-fearing; patient reliance on God would let Israel inherit the land held by Pharaoh's people.
rows.anchor: أن فرعون لا يملك الأرض حتى يمنحها من يشاء، ويمنع من التمتع بها من يشاء بل هي لله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The “outcome” is what follows a thing, opposite its beginning; it belongs to the God-fearing because God's ordering leads each kind to its created goal and happiness, and humans reach a wholesome life by following innate guidance and avoiding disbelief and corruption.
rows.anchor: العاقبة ما يعقب الشيء كالبادئة لما يبدء بالشيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Israel's “we were harmed before you came and after you came” uses synonymous “coming” and “arrival” for stylistic variety; adding “before the signs” is unsupported.
rows.anchor: الإتيان والمجيء في الآية بمعنى واحد، والاختلاف في التعبير للتفنن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their complaint is that Moses' arrival has not ended their continuing oppression despite the promised rescue; their point is not whether he brought signs, and they voice this grievance to him.
rows.anchor: فإن الأذى الذي كانوا يحملونه ويؤذون به على حاله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses consoles them with hope that God may destroy their enemy and make them successors, repeating the instruction to seek God and be patient; succession is a test of how they act, not an unconditional favor.
rows.anchor: ولا يصطفيكم بالاستخلاف اصطفاء جزافا، ولا يكرمكم إكراما مطلقا من غير شرط ولا قيد
